analyses.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The best risk/reward on the board: a memory supercycle inflection trading at 6.3x forward earnings with the stock still 20% below its high.

financials.summary: FY2025 was the year the memory cycle turned decisively in Micron's favour. After a loss-making FY2023 and a recovery FY2024, FY2025 delivered roughly $37B of revenue against about $25B the prior year — a ~49% increase — with gross margin expanding from the mid-20s to around 40% as DRAM and NAND pricing firmed and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI accelerators moved from pilot volumes to a material revenue line. Net income swung to roughly $8.5B, and the balance sheet strengthened enough to fund an aggressive capex program aimed almost entirely at HBM and leading-edge DRAM capacity. The trailing figures the scan picks up are even more dramatic (revenue +346%, EPS +1368% YoY) because they are measured against a depressed prior-year base — that is the signature of a cyclical inflection, not a steady-state growth rate.
highlights: Revenue approximately $37B in FY2025, up roughly 49% YoY
Net income approximately $8.5B, versus a near-breakeven FY2024
Gross margin expanded to roughly 40% from the mid-20s as pricing recovered
Diluted EPS in the mid-$7 range, from a fractional prior-year base
HBM became a material and rapidly scaling revenue line for AI accelerators
Scan-reported trailing growth: revenue +345.7% YoY, EPS +1368.5% YoY

accomplishments: Scaled HBM3E into volume production and secured multi-quarter supply agreements with AI accelerator customers
Moved to leading-edge DRAM nodes ahead of the schedule the market expected, closing the technology gap with Korean competitors
Sold out forward HBM capacity well in advance, converting a commodity business into a contracted one
Expanded US fabrication capacity supported by domestic semiconductor incentives
Returned to sustained GAAP profitability after the FY2023 downturn

journey_52w.summary: One of the most extraordinary 52-week runs of any large-cap in this scan: from a 52-week low of $115.60 to a high of $1213.37 — better than a ten-fold move — before settling at $971.66, about 19.9% below that peak. The advance was driven by the recognition that HBM turned memory from a commodity into a constrained, contracted input to AI infrastructure. The current position matters as much as the run: the stock has spent recent weeks building a base right on its 50-DMA at $960.65, digesting the move rather than breaking down, while the 200-DMA sits far below at $552.44.

analyses.name: Howmet Aerospace Inc.
analyses.verdict: The cleanest technical setup in the entire scan — pinned to its 52-week high with an RSI of just 51.2 — backed by real aerospace demand.

financials.summary: Howmet's FY2025 was a continuation of a multi-year margin transformation. Revenue grew to roughly $8.4B, up in the low-to-mid teens percent from about $7.4B, driven by commercial aerospace build rates recovering and, more importantly, by engine spares — the highest-margin part of the mix. The company's engineered castings and fastening systems sit on sole-source or dual-source positions on most modern engine platforms, which gave it genuine pricing power: margins expanded faster than revenue, with net income growing roughly 40%+ and EPS advancing to around the $3.9 area. Free cash flow supported both debt reduction and a materially increased buyback. The scan's trailing figures show revenue +24.1% and EPS +33.0% YoY, confirming the mix-driven leverage is still running.

analyses.name: Citigroup, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The cheapest money-center bank in a broad financial-sector uptrend, with quant and TradingView in rare full agreement.

financials.summary: FY2025 was the year Citigroup's long restructuring began showing up in returns rather than in charges. Revenue grew into the low-to-mid $80B range, up mid-to-high single digits, while expenses finally declined in absolute terms as the simplification program retired legacy businesses and headcount. The result was substantial operating leverage: net income advanced sharply and EPS grew into the $7-8 area from roughly $5.94 the prior year. Return on tangible common equity, the metric management is judged on, moved meaningfully toward its target for the first time in the plan's life. Markets and services revenue was the standout, while consumer banking benefited from resilient credit. The scan's trailing figures — EPS +61.0% and revenue +15.5% — capture how steep that operating leverage has become.

analyses.name: PNC Financial Services Group
analyses.verdict: A fresh 52-week high made on the lightest volume in the group — the quiet kind of breakout that tends to hold.

financials.summary: PNC's FY2025 was a clean regional-banking recovery year. Net interest income re-expanded as deposits repriced more slowly than assets, and fee income from asset management and capital markets grew alongside. Revenue advanced meaningfully — the scan's trailing figure shows +23.6% YoY — while credit costs stayed contained despite persistent market anxiety about commercial real estate exposure. Net income and EPS grew roughly a quarter year-over-year, capital ratios built comfortably above requirements, and the bank resumed a more assertive buyback. Crucially, PNC came through the regional-bank stress episodes of recent years as an acquirer of talent and deposits rather than a casualty, and that share gain is now visible in the revenue line.

analyses.name: Targa Resources, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The best-structured way to own energy right now — fee-based midstream cash flow with a chart that has digested, unlike the refiners.

financials.summary: Targa's FY2025 was defined by volume growth rather than commodity price. Permian gathering and processing throughput reached successive records as associated-gas production from oil drilling continued to rise, and the company's integrated NGL value chain — gathering, processing, fractionation, and export — captured margin at each stage. Revenue growth was modest at roughly 4% because commodity prices, which flow through the revenue line, were not the driver; earnings told the real story, with EPS up approximately 23% as fee-based volumes scaled against a largely fixed cost base. Major fractionation and pipeline projects were completed and placed in service, and the company continued to shift its contract mix toward fee-based structures that insulate cash flow from commodity swings.

analyses.verdict: At its 52-week high with RSI 57 and the lightest volume on the board — quiet strength with a live geopolitical tailwind.

financials.summary: General Dynamics delivered a broad-based FY2025 with all four segments contributing. Revenue grew roughly 8% to the high-$40B area, led by Marine Systems as submarine construction rates climbed under multi-year programs, and by Aerospace where Gulfstream deliveries of the newest large-cabin models finally normalized after a period of certification-driven delays. Combat Systems benefited from replenishment demand for munitions and vehicles, while Technologies grew steadily on government IT and mission-support contracts. EPS grew faster than revenue — approximately 13% — as Aerospace margins recovered with delivery volume. The backlog reached a record, providing multi-year revenue visibility that is unusual even by defense standards.

analyses.name: Ross Stores, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The highest-scoring consumer name in the scan and the most fully digested chart on the board — though TradingView is the least convinced of my STRONG BUYs.

financials.summary: Ross Stores turned in a strong fiscal 2025. Revenue grew roughly 20% to the low-$20B range, driven by comparable-store sales gains alongside continued unit expansion of both the Ross and dd's DISCOUNTS banners. The off-price model worked exactly as designed: an abundant supply of branded merchandise let buyers acquire quality inventory at favourable cost, which flowed through to merchandise margin. Operating margin expanded, and EPS grew approximately 37% — well ahead of revenue — reflecting that margin leverage plus buyback-driven share count reduction. Inventory turns stayed healthy, avoiding the markdown pressure that punishes retailers who misjudge demand.

analyses.name: Seagate Technology Holdings
analyses.verdict: The storage side of the AI-data buildout at 17.6x forward, carrying the highest TradingView buy count in this brief.

financials.summary: Seagate's FY2025 was a decisive cyclical recovery. After a brutal FY2023-24 trough in which the HDD industry ran well below normal demand, cloud and hyperscaler nearline drive orders returned in force — driven directly by the storage requirements of AI training data and inference archives. Revenue grew roughly 48% year-over-year, and because HDD manufacturing carries very high operating leverage, the earnings response was far larger: EPS grew approximately 149%. Gross margin expanded substantially as the mix shifted toward high-capacity nearline drives and as the company's HAMR (heat-assisted magnetic recording) technology began shipping in volume, giving it an areal-density advantage that competitors have struggled to match.

analyses.name: Digital Realty Trust, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The REIT route into the AI datacenter buildout — 29.9% revenue growth, un-extended chart, perfect TradingView card.

financials.summary: FY2025 was a landmark leasing year for Digital Realty. Revenue grew approximately 30% as record bookings — driven overwhelmingly by AI training and inference deployments requiring large contiguous power blocks — converted into commenced leases. Renewal spreads on expiring contracts turned sharply positive for the first time in years, because power-constrained supply gave landlords pricing leverage they had not had in a decade. The important caveat for reading the income statement: reported GAAP EPS declined sharply (the scan shows -58.7%), which is normal and expected for a REIT in a heavy development cycle, where depreciation and development expense weigh on net income while cash generation grows. Funds from operations, the metric that actually matters for REITs, moved in the opposite direction to GAAP earnings.
highlights: Revenue growth of approximately 29.9% YoY per trailing scan data
Record leasing bookings driven by AI training and inference deployments
Renewal spreads turned materially positive on power-constrained supply
GAAP EPS -58.7% YoY — a development-cycle artifact; assess FFO instead
Large development pipeline pre-leased ahead of delivery
Reported forward P/E of 69.2 on a GAAP basis, which materially overstates the true multiple

accomplishments: Achieved record annual leasing bookings, led by hyperscale AI deployments
Secured large contiguous power capacity in constrained metros — now the industry's binding resource
Turned renewal spreads positive after years of flat-to-negative re-leasing
Executed joint ventures and capital recycling to fund development without excessive dilution
Pre-leased a substantial portion of the forward development pipeline

analyses.name: Centene Corporation
analyses.verdict: A quiet, orderly margin recovery near its 52-week high at 12.7x forward, with a perfect zero-sell TradingView card.

financials.summary: Centene's FY2025 was a margin-repair year rather than a growth year. Revenue grew modestly — the trailing scan figure is 4.6% — as Medicaid membership stabilized following the multi-year redetermination process that had removed millions of members from the rolls sector-wide. The value was created below the top line: management focused on rate adequacy in state Medicaid contracts and on marketplace pricing discipline, accepting membership loss where rates were unacceptable. The medical loss ratio, the single metric that determines managed-care profitability, moved back toward target after a period of adverse cost trend, and administrative expense ratio discipline added further leverage. The result is a business earning materially more on a slowly growing revenue base.
highlights: Revenue growth of approximately 4.6% YoY — deliberately modest, prioritizing rate adequacy over membership
Medical loss ratio recovering toward target after adverse cost trend
Medicaid membership stabilized following the redetermination cycle
Marketplace pricing discipline restored segment profitability
Forward P/E of 12.7 — a low multiple for the recovery underway
Price rose from a 52-week low of $28.38 to $67.47 — a more than two-fold recovery

accomplishments: Restored the medical loss ratio toward target after a period of severe cost-trend pressure
Navigated the Medicaid redetermination cycle to membership stabilization
Repriced marketplace products for adequacy rather than chasing membership share
Exited or repriced unprofitable state contracts
More than doubled off the 52-week low as the market recognized the margin repair
